title: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

sense.text:
“The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, and with the point of a diamond: it is graven upon the table of their heart.” The sins of our people are so engraved in our minds that they are part of our makeup. The only way to fix that is for it to be beaten out with the word of God. The same way it was etched into our minds, we now have to be forceful with the word of God, so the people can understand the urgency of changing.

Many of us, when we first heard it, did not believe that God did not love everybody. The first thing that came to mind was that God so loved the world. Then the scriptures came out, and each of us came to the point of wrestling with ourselves: do I deny what I just read for myself and go with my thought, or do I submit to the word of God? He says he is the God of Israel and none else. A man can go on a journey from 1995 to prove that wrong and still not find a precept that says it is wrong. But the sins are so engraved in our minds.

That is especially so for us here in America, Babylon. All minds are fried. The witchcraft we call Christianity has messed us up, and the witchcraft we call democracy has messed us up. We think we have free will to do what we want; you have free will to die. With God there is only one way.

This is not a women-bashing class. The black woman is the white man’s lieutenant: she hates to hear it because she does not want to relinquish her power. But the class is more than her; the black man is in it too. In America, all minds are fried. Our people ignorantly hate the Bible, and in turn they hate us because we read the Bible. That is the condition of the battle. We do the work of the Most High and let him sort out the rest.

precepts.why: “The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” That is where we are: the land of the north. And in the land of the north, all of our minds are seared with a hot iron; all our minds are etched with sin. That is where the sin of Judah was written so deep.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee.” We are discontinued, disconnected, from this heritage and from the laws of God that make us a special people. So when we come to the people and tell them God only loves one people, it is hard for them to digest, because we do not know the laws of God and do not even know that the laws are important. There is push back because we are an unruly people. We do not like to be governed by the laws of God or told what we are doing right and wrong. The catchphrase is, No man can judge me, only God can judge me: the same old Christian BS.

Because we are disconnected, we lash out and build a hatred. Tell a brother he cannot sleep from woman to woman, cannot sell drugs, cannot murder his brother; tell a sister she cannot wear pants and is not equal to man; here comes the fight. That is because of verse four.

“I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” This is here, America. That fire in his anger is what caused us to go into captivity and be disconnected from the laws he gave us.

Forever means forever, but there is a caveat. That fire burns forever for those that rebel against the laws of God; they stay disconnected. But if you bethink yourself in the land where you were carried captive and repent, you will be delivered out of this land of the north. You are delivered by learning the laws of God. So do not let anyone trip you up into thinking forever means you will never come out. The prophets always spoke of the impending judgment, the judgment when it happened, and the deliverance God promised if we would repent. But two thirds of our people will not hear the law of the Lord. They hate it.

sense.text:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” This is where we take full swipes at Christianity, the religion, or better said the witchcraft of Christianity, because it does not teach you how to prepare yourself for temptation. It does not teach the laws of God. It just says believe in Jesus and you will be saved. That is absurd.

You can believe that the man Jesus Christ came on the earth and died, but believing is an action word. It is not just saying I believe. A man can believe that if he stops eating carbs he will lose weight; believe it all you want, unless you stop eating carbs you are not losing any weight.

The laws of God are not grievous. There is no law in the Bible impossible for us to keep: do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal. Other beliefs demand far harder things, like strapping a bomb to yourself or beating your own back with a chain. The biggest thing we have to do is fast for twenty-four hours. What is hard, women not wearing pants? The law is only hard to one who does not want to change. We are a rebellious people that will not hear the law of the Lord, and then we get mad and hate.

What separates the Christian church from the world? Not a damn thing. Tithing. At the blitz in Atlanta outside the 2819 Church event at State Farm Arena, you could not tell its members from people standing outside a Cardi B or Megan Thee Stallion concert. They were dressed the same, cutting lines, defrauding each other, wanting to fight. People were passing out in line, and nobody was there to help them but the prophets of the Lord. IUIC's medical team and hydration team stepped in and took care of the people, the same people who were cursing them out, because we love our people. Shame on Mr. Pam’s black backside, the false prophet: he did not even take care of the people coming to see him. We had to take care of his people.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Set your mind right: learn these laws, learn what the will of God is, and constantly endure. Trouble is going to come when you teach the word of God. It is impossible to teach this Bible and not expect trouble. This is not a Christian church; that is why they do not understand us. We are going to catch hell.

The men who marched in last week invoked the hatred against them. Many wanted to put hands on them, but the Lord protected his prophets and allowed them to teach the word. It was a bloodbath for Christianity: we came with scriptures, and all they could do was chant Jesus. For spiritual eyes, they scream in Jesus’ name, but what is screaming Lord, Lord, if you do not do the things he says? Christ said, If you love me, keep my commandments; they do not know that.

When Pam left his people out in despair, the word of God reached them anyway: a sister who stood in line at 2819 heard the brothers walking with authority, took a pamphlet, and came to the class.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.” Before it said prepare thy soul; here it says cleave unto him. You cleave unto the Most High by diligently keeping his commandments. When trials come, they come for us, and it is the laws of God that activate in our minds and tell us we can endure this. It will not be easy, but it will be okay. At the end, we win.

The increase at the last end is getting the kingdom. That is why we endure hardship, and why we are not worried about what the people out there say or do. What drives this truth is knowing that at the end we are going to rule over the nations. We are going to take them captive that took us captive. We know the atrocities our people suffered, slavery and the police beatings; so we keep his laws, and now it turns around. You reap what you sow. It was all right for us to go into captivity; why is it not all right for you to go?

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Why must we take it cheerfully and be patient? Verse three just said it: that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.

When we come into this truth we do not know how emotional we are from being raised in Christianity. Christianity bred an emotional generation of black men, and it trickled down to gang violence, where the only way we know to resolve a conflict is to move with action. You do not know those things are inside you until the laws are introduced into your life. That is why whatever is brought upon you, take it cheerfully: these impurities are brought to the forefront by the laws of God. The situations arise for us to see the people for who they are, but also to see you for who you are.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” Gold, when it goes through the fire, has all its impurities burned out. To be accepted by God, we have to go through adversities. It is part of the makeup; it is the condition of our battle. So when we go out there we are not confused that the people will turn against us, that the government will be against us, that we will be hated. We understand that.

The beta male of the Christian church is not like that. He wants everybody to get along and shake his neighbor’s hand, and all you have to do is sing soprano and everything will be all right. That will not bring about Christ’s kingdom. Christ’s kingdom comes with death. Judgment has to come, blood has to spill, people have to be in derision. People do not want that; they want to stay comfortable, just as it was when we came out of Egypt.

precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord.” That is how you prepare your heart: to seek the law of the Lord. Read on: “and to do it.” You can seek and search the scriptures for the laws of the Lord, but until you do it, you have not prepared yourself. It is an action word; it is a verb.

“And to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” So to prepare yourself for the temptation to come, you have to seek the law, you have to do the law, and then you have to teach the law. That is the fullness of preparing yourself. When you are teaching the law, you are rehearsing it over and over: telling somebody, Do not commit adultery, you are teaching yourself the same thing at the same time.

“Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men.” If you are preparing yourself, seeking the law, doing the law and teaching the law, you must not be a hypocrite in the sight of men. “And take good heed what thou speakest”: make sure what you are speaking is according to the Bible.

On the streets people walk up and say, So you are telling me you are not sinning? Do not be a hypocrite; you say, No, I am keeping the Sabbath, I am not committing adultery, I am not murdering. They say it is impossible because they really do not want to prepare themselves for the Lord.

The Christian church literally believes it can do anything it wants and the Lord is pleased with it. This was spoken to our forefathers in their folly, but it is the Christian church today: “Behold, ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit.” Not only this one self-proclaimed pastor; there are many others outside the 2819 Church. The issue is that the people are not studying and holding these pastors accountable. You need to study for yourself so you can figure out what is right and what is wrong.

“Will ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not; And come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?” That is what the Christian church does: they keep no laws and tell you God is okay with it. That is what you are saying when you say the law is done away with. They say the law is fulfilled, but they do not understand grammar: if you fulfill the law, you do it, you keep it.

That is called, I am under grace. But think of a grace period on a light bill: it is given so you end up paying it, not so you keep on being delinquent.

Verse three: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.” To amend is to change and to fix. The Lord wants us to change.

“For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.” The people are supposed to be seeking the law at the priest’s mouth. So if a man says he is a messenger, a priest, a bishop, representing God on earth to lead you to the kingdom, he should know the laws of God, and you are supposed to challenge him: ask him questions about what is necessary for salvation, how to get saved.

We say this with all sincerity, because these are our people; we love them and want to see them come to repentance. But you will not know whether what he says is correct if you do not study to show thyself approved and know the laws. That is why they have a problem with us. The mega pastors will let the people from their congregations come outside and talk, but they want no part of us themselves.

The pastors will not come out to us, because we open the Bible, take them into deep waters and watch them drown. A man setting up a Christmas tree in December does not know the first thing about how to serve God. A man who talks slick about the Hebrew Israelites and then will not come out when we pull up, not for a fight but to talk the Bible: Oh, this nigga’s a punk. You lost me right then and there; do not follow him. They do not know the Bible; they hate God.

How do you cleave unto the Most High? “But take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, which Moses the servant of the Lord charged you, to love the Lord your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.”

You cleave unto God by diligently seeking his commandments. So when it says prepare your heart, prepare your heart in the law; cleave diligently unto the laws of God. We cannot define God’s words. God defines his own words and tells us what he means behind them. When we prepare ourselves for temptation, we learn these laws and cleave to them.

This is the increase at the last end, and this is why we do it: “And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath unto their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.” The Lord said he will increase us.

“And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.” That is why we endure temptation and hardship: at the end we receive the kingdom.

“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin.” That is all the impurities of sin in us, the same impurities the fire burns out of the gold.

“And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness.” To purge away our dross he restores the judges, and these judges will teach the laws to purify us, cleanse us and get us right, so that we can stand back up and rule.

But there will be a negro who has a problem with that. They trust in oppression and love it the way it is. We are so beaten down we do not realize there is something better. We are at the bottom with nothing to lose, so let Trump keep doing what he is doing: watch America implode on itself. A kingdom divided cannot stand, and America is divided, white against white. There is nothing like Esau showing you his true nature. Only Christianity gets you to love a person who keeps killing you and tells you everything is going to be all right.

“Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” We must, through much tribulation, enter. There is no other way. There must be tribulation to enter into the kingdom; that is why it says prepare your soul.

Young men who have not yet gone out to camp should look at what those men are doing and say, That is what I aspire to. Older men who cannot go out to camp had better find their place and put their hand to this plow. Do not be a brother or a sister who is here with nothing to do. God did not call you to this without you offering something on some level: some gift, some wisdom from your life and work that can help build. Nobody can say he is useless to this truth.

“Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” With great labor God formed us to come to this truth. Before we were born we were already formed to be in this; every one of us was ordained to be where we are today.

But let them perish who live a life born in vain, who bring nothing. He formed you perfect to do his work, and you bring nothing to him: that is a sad, cursed life, a life with no meaning. You can go to the Christian church and sit in the pew till you are eighty, but that cannot be named among us.

sense.text: “False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not.” A woman from the 2819 Church went on TikTok and said the scriptures we read justify pedophilia. She gave no verse. It is a lie, an agenda pushed to debunk what we truly teach, which is: brothers, marry your wives and take care of your families. Anyone who believes that has never heard us teach. As hard as we go for the laws of God, nobody sitting among these men could ever teach that it is all right to sleep with children; the brothers would drag him off the mic before the class was finished. They rise up against us as false witnesses to smear our name, all because we teach the laws of God. That is why we must stay honest and godly and not move in the spirit of hypocrisy. The goddamn black woman strikes again. Big mouth. The same woman gave the finger to Captain Shamaya while he was teaching on abortion.

“They rewarded me evil for good to the spoiling of my soul.” We were out there helping the people who were falling out from dehydration, the same people who were cursing us out. We gave them water and medical help. Where was Pam? That is the lieutenant right there. And still they turn on us, because of the laws of God. They are afraid when they see black men in power. They should be afraid, because we are not going anywhere.

“But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting.” We pray for them, we are out there trying to help and relieve them. “I behaved myself as though he had been my friend or brother.” You are our brothers and sisters; we do not hate you.

“But in mine adversity they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together.” They are waiting for the day they can rejoice over our falling. Some of these Christians were praying for our deaths. A father, mother and son came up to the camp, got on their knees and prayed against us while the word was taught, the boy looking so uncomfortable it looked like child abuse, the father going as far as prostrating himself on the hot ground.

That is why it is better to deal with gangbangers than with Christian people. The people on the corners, in their broken state, are more reasonable than the church folks. Church folk have pulled guns on us.

precepts.why:
On July 31, 2022, IUIC Minneapolis taught outside New Salem Missionary Baptist Church and was invited back the next week to sit down with the pastor. When the brothers returned on August 7, 2022, unarmed, men from the church met them with weapons, and one pulled out a pistol. Shame on that evil pastor. Reading the Bible escalated to firearms.

This is what it means to prepare your soul for temptation and adversity: “They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.” These negroes really think they are doing God service. You will never see us approach anybody with weapons over reading the Bible. If they did not want us there, all they had to do was go back in the church and close the doors, or call the police. But they were willing to take a man’s life, leave a wife without a husband and children without a father, over Bible verses.

They are lunatics, and they hate the word of God. They do not hate us; they hate Christ. They do not want to be told the words of God.

sense.text: “If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.” If you faint when adversity comes, if you give up, it shows that your faith was small. These situations arise to show you for who you are.

“If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain.” To forbear is to restrain, to avoid, to leave off. If thou avoid to deliver them that are drawn unto death. Put it simply: if we are on the corners and people are trying to kill us, and you leave us, you do not believe this Bible. That is not how this goes. We all come, we all leave, or nobody leaves. It is not about saving yourself and leaving your brother behind.

“If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not.” Oh, we did not know, was it that serious? “Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it?” God is pondering your heart and saying, You knew, but you left your brother. “And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?” You knew they were trying to kill him, and in adversity your faith was small; you were worried about being put to death. Do not fear them that can kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. You were worried about the wrong one.

precepts.why:
Some of the other Israelite camps say we should not be blitzing the churches; their ministry is TikTok and YouTube, talking to a camera in the middle of nowhere. That is not what we do. We go out there for the love of the people, to find them and bring the word to them.

“And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God. But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them.” Some of our people were hardened and spoke evil of what he was teaching. “And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus.” He still taught regardless.

Verse 19: “Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.” Because of the constant teaching, even with people who turned with an evil heart, the people destroyed their pagan books, worth what would be millions today.

It had to be a real sum, because it set their trade in danger: “So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.” Ephesus was a tourist spot; they sold their idols and their books, and this man turned it upside down. Some of the people were hardened, so he separated them: we will work with these, because those are no good. That is your church folks and your pastors today. We will work with some of the people from the 2819 Church, but others will turn and join with the white man against us like the coons they are.

What happens when we teach this word and people stop tithing, stop eating pork, women stop wearing pants, men stop wearing dresses, people stop stealing and murdering? When we affect the economy, they will come. We have not yet seen the wrath of Esau. That is when they will try to put us to death, and some brothers will find out how small their faith is.

“And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.” Full of wrath means violence; to take them they had to restrain them and hit them.

“And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.” Paul did not run and leave them; he tried to go in after his brother. “And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.” Paul understood he could not leave his brother out there facing death. He signed up for this knowing he could lose his life, and we signed up knowing we can never leave a brother out there. This is the condition of the battle.

The people last week were close to erupting; God held them off. They have a disdain for the strong, righteous, alpha black man. They will take the alpha male from prison, but not us. They hate us, and that is okay.

This should be the mindset, because we know it is going to happen. At the event it was mainly black women out there, and the first thing you felt was the hatred they had for us.

“And to him they agreed: and when they had called the apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.” The scribes and Pharisees set it up to beat those men for speaking Christ. That is what we teach, so the same things are going to happen.

“And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name. And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.” Even with the persecution, our job is to keep preaching Christ to our people. We have seen things in Kenya and other places; men at camp have had their lives threatened and guns pulled at the churches. If you are fearful of the thought of it, then when it happens you will run. Get your mind and spirit prepared now, because it is coming.

What brings on fear? Unbelief. And what brings on unbelief? Sin.

“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.” Those days are coming. “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord. They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” They will not spare woman, child or man; if it were up to them, and Christ did not cut it short, they would kill us all off. “For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They will take away your goods and your homes. That is why it says prepare your hearts: this is coming.

“And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” They are going to have a problem with us. They make war with the remnant that keeps the commandments; that is where the trouble of the insurrection in 2 Esdras 16 comes from.

Who is going to fear the trouble? “Behold, God himself is the judge, fear him: leave off from your sins, and forget your iniquities, to meddle no more with them for ever: so shall God lead you forth, and deliver you from all trouble.” When you leave your sins, God will deliver you.

When the trouble happens in the streets and they are trying to kill the brothers, the man in sin is afraid, because he knows he will not be delivered from the trouble; he is afraid that if he dies like this he will not inherit the kingdom. So he will not lay it all on the line. He falls back and tucks back, and will not do the work. We have to be sincere in this truth, repenting and leaving off sin, so that we can actually do the work, because the trial is coming and some men will be found of little faith. Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the face; all of us, the Bishop included, will be tried against what we say.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities.” Destruction to them that are bound with their sins: that is why you are afraid, because you are wrapped up in your sin. A present-day unrepentant fornicator trying to go out to camp should stay home and get that fixed first; save yourself the problem.

But verse 75: “Be ye not afraid neither doubt.” When you are right, you will not be afraid. An instinct kicks in to do the work. That does not mean a level of fear will not hit you, but it will not cripple you. Bravery is found in fear, in overcoming your fear and doing the work. It is easy to march with a hundred men; the days are coming when it is just you and a reader. Those in active sin, unrepentant, are the ones to be afraid of being around.

sense.text:
“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more.” Even though they were beaten and thrown into prison in Acts 5, they were not going to be moved off the corner. We are not shutting up and we are not changing what we teach; this is what we signed up for. Lock us up, and there will be an IUIC San Quentin; the teaching will not stop. Kill us, and the next powerful teachers will rise up to teach the word.

What keeps us is that we know we are coming back. If you do not believe that, being put to death for this truth, you will be resurrected in that day, your faith is small, and that is why you will not do it. We believe a big black man is going to come out of the sky with angels to deliver us. They believe in a fat white man coming down a chimney to a Christmas tree.

“But thine eyes shall see thy teachers.” You will see us. We are on the corners; we are everywhere.
“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.” That is our job: to tell the people, This is the way. Come out of those churches. The real Jews are black.

precepts.why: This is the same thing we read in Acts: “Thus saith the king, Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.” That was the charge for teaching the word of God: lock him up. And when he comes out, he teaches the word of God again. That is the bread of adversity and the water of affliction of Isaiah 30:20, and still the teachers are not removed into a corner.

“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death.” Some of us will be cast into prison, some will die in prison, some will be put to death. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved. “Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.”

Could this be read in the Christian church and accepted? Oh, I have to die for this, I have to go to prison? They are not the people. They do not see death or imprisonment as what is coming to obtain the kingdom, they do not see the much tribulation. They think you shake your neighbor’s hand, give tithes, and wake up walking with lambs and lions. What Disney show are you watching? They love smooth words; they think it will be soft and cushy. Which Christian church teaches that you have to die for this gospel? None. If they taught that, the people would rip out of the church. Creflo, TD, Juanita: they are getting bought off.

sense.text:
Why are we going to be thrown in prison and put to death? What will we do that makes him so mad? Here is the reason: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie.” The Most High is the author of beauty and made everything; and out of all the people he created, that is supposed to be his best creation? No.

In 2025, who would believe the Jews are white? You could look it up and find out the Jews are black. Their own writers write that these people are converts, transplants, counterfeits; it is not secret information, it is on Amazon. You are a counterfeit, a fake; you are not the Jew. And when we tell our people that they are the Jews, they do not want to hear it, because these fake lying pastors have sold them out.

The politicians are bought off too. Shontel Brown, the Democrat from Ohio, supports the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Israel, and took over $13,000 of AIPAC money. Hakeem Jeffries, the Democrat from New York, supports Israel’s effort to defend itself. Ritchie Torres, who took over $500,000 from AIPAC, defends them and will not call it genocide. Even granting that October 7 happened, and Esau will set up a problem to bring the solution, the response was to kill over 70,000 people, women and children. These people are natural born killers. Amalek has a problem with what is called genocide, and this sellout negro defends it, when he should mind his business and worry about his people here. These are the so-called leaders, and when we call them out, we are the bad guys. No problem. That is the price we chose. We are not keeping quiet.

“Behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.” They will know they call themselves the Jews and are not, and they will become our servants.

precepts.why: It says they are counterfeits: “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits.” We esteem you as counterfeits. You are not the Jews. The Jews are black.

sense.text:
Them knowing that, and hearing that, back to chapter 2: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich).” God knows the tribulation and the poverty we are going through, but we are rich with the word of God. We are not physically rich; we are broke, with no money to buy off politicians.

“And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” The blasphemy is the lie of the counterfeits.

“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer.” We are going to suffer for identifying that they are not the Jews, that they are counterfeits. You think they are over there killing Ishmael and are not coming for us? They will turn their attention and say, You are next. We did not forget you: we will take your homes, throw you in prison and kill you. They have no conscience; we are cattle to them, and they will kill women and children. But it is all right.

precepts.why: What are we rich with? “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs.” Why teach one another in psalms and spiritual songs? Because the repetition of a song helps you memorize. The psalm of being happy when the little ones are dashed against the stones is a song we could sing all day; it reminds us of what the Lord said, that they will come and worship before thy feet. That is the word of God dwelling richly in you.

sense.text: “I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” That open door is the door of utterance, the door of speech. He taught us this word, and now we are not going to keep quiet. Whether the people hear or forbear, we will do our job and let the rest fall where it falls.

precepts.why: “Withal praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of utterance, to speak the mystery of Christ.” The mysteries of Christ are to speak this Bible, and the Lord opens to us a door of utterance. “For which I am also in bonds”: I am in bonds to speak this word, I cannot stop speaking it; I am a prisoner of Christ. This is what we signed up for. There is no looking back and saying this is not for me; then the kingdom is not for you either. The word of God dwells richly in us to teach this word and tell the truth of this Bible, with no changes.

This goes along with the fire within us. We have to have the spirit that will not cease teaching this Bible no matter what comes before us: persecution, threats, jail.

“And the next day, behold, a voice called me, saying, Esdras, open thy mouth, and drink that I give thee to drink. Then opened I my mouth, and, behold, he reached me a full cup, which was full as it were with water, but the colour of it was like fire. And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.” As Christ promised in John 14, the Comforter brings all things to remembrance.

“And my mouth was opened, and shut no more.” It could not be silenced no matter what was before it. We are not shutting up. Remove one of us and there is another brother right behind doing the same thing; you would have to get rid of all of us, and that is not going to happen. This word does not go out void. In Cuba, when they came with clubs and a bus to take the brothers, as soon as one was taken another took up the mic.

sense.text: “O Lord, thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived: thou art stronger than I, and hast prevailed.” Thy will, Father, is stronger than I; it is going to compel me. “I am in derision daily, every one mocketh me.” He was mocked and went through much tribulation for teaching this word. He is saying, I was deceived; I thought it was going to be easy, and I learned it is not.
“Because the word of the Lord was made a reproach unto me, and a derision, daily.” For teaching this word he was mocked and reproached daily.

“Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” I am catching too much hell; I will not mention this anymore or speak in his name. “But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones.” It was etched into his mind; he could not help it. That is why you cannot turn back now: you have already heard this word. If the spirit of God is in you, it burns in you. Even when you feel you are going through too much, it will eat you alive that you want to do the work, and even though you are afraid, you will do it.

“And I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” Forbearing is being restrained. He was weary with holding back from teaching; he could not stay, because the word was in him and he could not keep quiet. The door of utterance was given to him, and it was impossible not to teach. That is the spirit we have to have.

“For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” “All my familiars watched for my halting”: all of our people are waiting for us to fall so they can talk. That is why we had better be blameless in this truth; they hope to find some smut to say we are evil. “Saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.” Perhaps he will be enticed to sin against God, and then they have a reason to mock: look at this hypocrite, that Israelite stuff is BS. Let it not be named among us.

precepts.why:
How was he deceived? “Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel.” “Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.” When we first heard this word it was sweet. We first heard that we are the Israelites, that Christ only died for us, and could not put the book down; the Bible got wrinkled in the bed because we read until we fell asleep. Our whole world changed.

Then the words started getting bitter. We might die, we might go to jail, we might lose wives, children and friends. We cannot smoke weed, there is no precept for it. If we sneak and do these things, eternal damnation. The word of God constrains us, and at the end we may lose our lives behind this truth. It seems good when you first hear it, then you hear the severity.

The severity: a woman tried to run the brothers over with her car for reading the Bible. Brothers lost their jobs after last week’s blitz when their employers saw it, men with wives, children and mortgages. Every time we go out, our lives are on the line. So in camp, especially in tight quarters, pay attention, get off the phone, and always watch a person’s hands and eyes; they will tell you what he is about to do.

“And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter. And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” John was on the isle of Patmos, in prison; he already knew the bitterness of the word. He is speaking of this time: we are coming back to do the same thing again, to teach the people whether they hear or forbear, and to be cast into prison, put to death, beaten, and lose homes and jobs. This is the condition of the battle. We will travel the world to preach before nations, tongues and kings.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” God knew us before he formed us; we were chosen. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet.” None of us is here by chance. It is ordained of God that in our time we would be woken up to who we are in the truth. Now that we know it, we have to get ourselves right and go out and find the people and bid them to this wedding. That is why we are on the corners and why we travel the world: to do the work God called us to do. We were ordained to be prophets.

“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” Appointed to death. Look at these Power Rangers walking the streets in order, they say; they think we are clowns, not knowing they are witnessing the sons of God back on the earth.

“We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong.” The people will be made wise and strong in Christ by what we teach. “Ye are honourable, but we are despised.”

“Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace.” These men were ostracized and called fools for teaching this word, lost everything and had no certain dwelling place. “And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it.” We hold jobs; we are not sitting here collecting tithes to pay our bills. Their pastors are not on the front line; the only time they come out is to collect money or for a photo op. And people ask why we march instead of helping in Chicago; we have already been there.

“Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.” We have been called sellouts, witches, pedophiles, wife abusers, gay; we are looked at as the filth of the world.

“I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you.” Prepare your soul for temptation and tribulation; this is what you signed up for. “For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.” Paul was beaten and imprisoned, and says follow the example I set; he asked nothing he had not gone through. We ask the men to go out there, and there is nothing we are not doing or have not done. In Orlando, years ago, there was nowhere to stand, no foot traffic and no reader but a six-year-old son; the word was taught to the buses, the bus stop and the parking lots. The word does not go out void: today Orlando, Miami, Tallahassee, Jacksonville and Tampa are full of Israelites.

“I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.” They laugh at us. A young brother says he is a virgin and they ask if he is gay. They laugh us to scorn: you are the prophets in that outfit, looking like a Power Ranger, with that beard? You are nobody.

sense.text: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate.” That is our people. We go to the front line and rebuke the people: sister, you cannot go from man to man; brothers, you cannot go from woman to woman; you cannot be a thief. They hate us for telling them the laws of God, and that is how we know we are the people of God. People hate correction. “And they abhor him that speaketh uprightly”: they abhor him that speaks the laws of God.

precepts.why: What is uprightly? “My son, be mindful of the Lord our God all thy days, and let not thy will be set to sin, or to transgress his commandments: do uprightly all thy life long.” Uprightly is keeping the commandments: living by the laws of God. So they abhor him that speaks the laws of God.

“Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?” We become the enemies of our people because we tell them the laws of God. They have hatred toward us for teaching them what is good for them. When the brothers went to Kenya and told the people God loves you, you are made after his image, you are a special people, they stoned them. That mind is gone. Imagine if they had been rebuked from the scriptures. We are a hateful people that hate the word of God.

sense.text:
“And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” Christ died, and they went out and taught. They loved not their lives because they preached the testimony.

They made war with us and hated us because we knew we were the children of Israel and that we would receive the kingdom, and we taught our people: you are the children of Israel, and the kingdom is yours. The enemy is wroth with that.

And our people say, What about the white man? Amalek never asks, What about the black people in America? No Chinese man does that; we are the only people. There is no greater witchcraft than Christianity. They say all nations can be saved, everybody gets the kingdom. Then what is the benefit of keeping the commandments? No pork, no weed, no fornicating, no robbing, no clubs, and at the end all I get is unlimited watermelon and no work, and the white man who killed me gets the same thing? Why would he want to be friends with me there if he was not here? Who taught you that religion? Your slave master. If I were a slave master I would have taught you the same thing; he is doing his job. It is the negroes who refuse to hear the truth of this Bible.

precepts.why:
What testimony were they preaching? “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.”

“For the Lord hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.” We desire it: to sit upon a throne for evermore. The Lord has chosen Zion, us. So the testimony we preach is that we will sit upon a throne for evermore, for the Lord has chosen us. He said, Come unto me, you heavy laden, I will give thee rest. We want that rest.

sense.text:
There has to be something more than the white man getting the same reward.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom.” That is why they have an issue with the purple and gold. When they see us stand up on our feet, they see God’s kingdom, and it lets them know their kingdom is coming to an end. “Which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people.” Our kingdom is not going to be left to other people; it is only for us. Stop including the white man. The blessings are for the sons of Jacob.

The Edomite evangelist out of Austin, Texas, says if slavery never happened black people would be living in grass huts, that our reparations are that we get to live in America, you’re welcome, that we got the Christian religion, and that the best moment in history for any brown or black country is when the white man’s ships arrive on its shores, bringing the gospel so we can go to heaven instead of hell. So we catch hell here on earth and then must go live with the same people in heaven? That is why our people always bring up the oppressor when we teach that the kingdom is for them: in their minds Christ is white, and the ones who taught them Christianity are white. And he says there were mistakes on both sides, when they stole us from a whole country and brought us here as slaves.

precepts.why:
The Christian church has blurred the lines between what is clean and unclean, and that has our people in the stupor they are in. “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” Christians do not understand that you will pay for what you do in this body. They say, You cannot judge me. True, we are not the final judge, but the Lord is sending prophets to warn you that everybody must sit before that judgment seat.

“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” God knows my heart why I smoked weed, why I wear pants: the Lord is going to destroy you. The watchmen of the churches are not warning the people, so we have to have that fire in our bones, knowing the terror of the Lord our people face blindly, and persuade them to stop breaking God’s laws. Our people will be on fire forever because they are trying to save the white man. Nobody ever asks, What about the African, or the Chinese man; it is always Esau by default.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.” We are made manifest by everything just read in Corinthians: losing homes and families for what we teach. What pastor loses his home for what he teaches? We see the bishops, the deacons and the captains traveling all over; that is manifest where the word of God is. Know who your brothers are and follow the example.

Because they are two-time losers, they want us to be losers too. But the kingdom is for us and only us.

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after death to look for punishment?” What profit is it for us to live in hell right now, getting up for our nine to fives while the white man oppresses our people and kills us in the streets? Who gets the true punishment? Our enemies get the punishment for what they have done to us. That is why they want to keep us in sin, teach us a false Christ, and say the laws are done away with: they know they are going into captivity and will be destroyed, and they want to take us down with them.

The hypocrite must be stopped: the hypocrisy of saying there were mistakes on both sides. Yes, we sinned against our God, and he sent the nations to enslave us, but they went too far, they furthered the affliction, and there will be a judgment for their wrongdoing.

“Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth, That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment?” He will not admit the atrocities they did to God’s people, because if he admits it he understands there must be judgment and recompense behind it: his kingdom has to come to an end. The only way to right those wrongs is for him to go into slavery and for us to go into rulership.

“Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds; Yet he shall perish for ever.” Going up to the space station: who fits that description? Your friendly neighborhood white man. And he shall perish for ever.

sense.text:
“And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The Most High considers what we go through, slavery, being put to death, prison, a little chastisement. Afterward we receive the reward, but we have to go through it. It is the only way to get what we are looking for, salvation and eternal life. We have to risk it all and believe.

It comes back to faith, and faith is tied directly to keeping the commandments. To have good understanding you must keep the laws; in keeping the laws your understanding grows and your faith grows, and you believe what you are reading. That is the only way we will endure: knowing that whatever happens to us, if we lose our lives in this time, we will be back.

precepts.why:
See the mindset of our forefathers, how they thought. “So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” His understanding and his faith said it is good to lose my life being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again, knowing that Christ holds the keys of hell and death.

“As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.” As for you, Esau, you will have no resurrection to life. Those left behind will be servants until their time is fulfilled, and all the nations that took part in this will serve us. But there is a price for that: we have to be hated by nations and hated by our own, and we will receive eternal life.

sense.text:
“These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.”

The palm is a sign of victory, of achievement. That is what we all want: to say we got that crown, we got that palm, we were clothed in white, we stood stiffly for the name of God.

“What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands? So he answered and said unto me, It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.” What Ezra was seeing was us in the last days, what we went through. These are the men who stood stiffly in the face of being put to death and imprisoned. They did not give up and did not hold their tongues; they spoke the word. That is why, brothers, stay in the scriptures as it is written: he that leads into captivity shall go into captivity.

precepts.why: The palms are seldom explained. “Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Reuben were sealed twelve thousand”, and so through all the tribes of Israel to Benjamin. “After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands; And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.” Those are the same palms given to us in 2 Esdras 2:45.

“Flee the shadow of this world, receive the joyfulness of your glory: I testify my Saviour openly. O receive the gift that is given you.” The ones crowned and given palms are the ones who received this gift.
What is the gift given us? “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life.” The gift of God is eternal life.

Some will die. But if they die, what then? “And those that be dead will I raise up again from their places, and bring them out of the graves: for I have known my name in Israel.” That is what we have to believe: for teaching this word we are going to be hated, and they are going to come against us and kill us. But that is the only way this gospel will get heard, by us forcing this word down people’s throats to hear it.

sense.text: Zedekiah “humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord.” We had those men who would not hear when Jeremiah spoke from the word of God.

“Moreover all the chief of the priests, and the people, transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen; and polluted the house of the Lord.” Many of the priests turned from God, like the churches today. How can the priests of the Christian church today celebrate Christmas? Do not tell me they never heard Jeremiah 10. They have perverted their ways from God.

“And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people.” Today God has compassion on his people, and that compassion is shown in sending us out.

“But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” There will be a day when the people start looking for this word and it will not be found; we will no longer be teaching it to them like that. They will have to go through this judgment and accept that they chose wrong. Until then, we do our work. We will be hated for this, but do not worry: at the end, we win.
